memory_candidates.content: lint-postflight-boundary.sh's violation scanner sets in_postflight=1 at any heading matched by /^#{2,4} .*Postflight/ (or a numbered Stage pattern) and keeps printing subsequent lines for the build-command/grep/mcp__ pattern checks until it hits a heading matching ^## Return Format|^## Error Handling|^## MUST NOT — regardless of intervening heading LEVEL. So content under a 3-hash heading added after an existing postflight section (e.g. skill-orchestrate/SKILL.md's Move 4 and a hypothetical Move 5) is scanned under the SAME violation window as the postflight section itself, even though it is textually and semantically a separate stage. Two practical consequences: (1) a new ###-level addition after a postflight heading must independently avoid build-command/grep-on-source/mcp__ patterns, it does not get a free pass just because it's a new heading; (2) content placed inside a '## MUST NOT (...)' heading IS excluded from the scan (the awk stop condition fires exactly at that heading), which is the safe place to put cross-reference prose that would otherwise need pattern-avoidance scrutiny.

This repo enforces per-file context-budget ceilings on skills/skill-orchestrate/SKILL.md (21,500 B) and commands/orchestrate.md (21,000 B) via context/config/orchestrator-context-budget.json, checked by verify-deploy.sh gate 20. Headroom on both files is now very thin (24 B and 29 B respectively after this task). The established, repeatedly-applied convention when a legitimate new feature needs documentation space in either file: compact the NEW prose first (iteratively, checking `wc -c` after each edit), and only as a last resort compact an adjacent PRE-EXISTING paragraph too — never request a ceiling move until compaction is genuinely exhausted (every prior ceiling move in this file's own history records at least one real compaction attempt first). A ceiling move, when truly needed, is 'reviewed, dated', recorded in the config file's own derivation field, and rounds up to the next 500 B boundary.

A new .sh script created via the Write tool has mode 100644 (not executable) — Write never sets the execute bit. Every manual verification that invokes it as `bash <script>` will succeed regardless, masking the gap, but tests/run-all.sh's suite discovery checks `[ -x "$f" ]` before running a discovered file directly and loudly [SKIP]s a non-executable one as an 'exec-bit regression'. Always `chmod +x` a newly created shell script (both the source-store copy and, if manually smoke-tested pre-deploy, the deployed copy) and confirm with a DIRECT execution (`./script.sh ...` or `$PWD/script.sh`), not only a `bash`-prefixed invocation, before considering the script's creation step done.
